pick.headline: Polish television reports an NKVD execution site for Polish prisoners of war
pick.summary: On March 22, 1990, Polish television's main news reported the discovery of an execution site in the Turza woods in Poland where, it said, the NKVD, the Soviet secret police, had shot Polish prisoners in August to October 1944, after the Soviet Army entered the area.
pick.significance: For half a century Moscow had blamed the Nazis for the murder of thousands of Polish officers at Katyn in 1940. Reports like this one, possible only after Poland's 1989 change of government, came weeks before the Soviet Union admitted, on April 13, 1990, that the NKVD had carried out the Katyn killings.
pick.fbis: The East Europe report of March 23, 1990, carried Warsaw PAP in English under the FBIS heading 'Another NKVD Crime' Uncovered: Polish TV had reported an execution site in the Turza woods, used by the NKVD from August to October 1944 and known locally as a 'Small Katyn.'

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: East Europe, No. 057, 23 March 1990
evidence.snippet: …arsaw, March 22—An execution site where Polish POWs were murdered by the NKVD [People’s Commissariat of Internal Affairs] was discovered in the woods in Turza near the former POWs’ camp in Trze- buszka, the main TV news bulletin reported tonight. The executions took place from mid-August to mid- October 1944 after the Soviet Army had entered these lands. At that time the Turza woods took on the name of a “Small Katyn.”
